claims.assertion: The trip ran 10.9 km against a 7.9 km optimal route (+3.0 km, +38%) and included one off-route segment 18:32–18:39 that drove 3.32 km where the optimal route covers 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km and straying up to 1262 m from the optimal route.

The driver asked at 18:28 'ok if I go round via Outram Road?' and the rider never replied; under RD-5 an unanswered route-change proposal is not consent, and the request timestamp precedes the off-route segment's start, so the segment is not exempted.

The driver's written justification ('no objection, so I took it') rests only on the rider's silence, which contradicts the chat record showing no rider agreement message at all; silence does not satisfy 'reach a mutual agreement before you go'.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only speed-band readings (New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway, band 3 = 20–29 km/h) are not on the substituted optimal route at band 1 or 2, so no RD-4 exemption applies to the unexempted segment.

RydeTAXI bills by the meter, so the 2.21 km of unexempted deviation distance is chargeable detour mileage; at this trip's own per-km rate (distance fare $15.33 ÷ 10.9 km = $1.4064/km) the refund is 2.21 × $1.4064 ≈ $3.11, and the rider's recoverable excess distance billed is $4.21 (3.0 km × $1.41/km).
The complaint is timely and 30 days have not elapsed, and the refund is payable as a Ryde voucher per NS-7.
The driver's account (185 days old, rating 4.5, 2 disputes in 90 days) shows no upheld route dispute, so the additional flag_account of RD-6 is not triggered here.

weaknesses: RD-2's non-metered/metered split hinges on the service being RydeTAXI; if the trip were re-classified as a fixed-quote service, the recoverable amount would fall to the ERP/toll excess on the deviation segment only (F4, F6).

The deviation is a single 7-minute segment in an area with heavy evening congestion (F11 shows no incidents, but F9/F10 show band 3 roads at 20–29 km/h near the corridor); the driver may argue some of the extra distance was unavoidable (F8, F9, F11).

The +3.0 km total excess exceeds the 2.21 km of the single off-route segment by ~0.79 km, and the driver could argue the remainder falls within map-matching residue rather than an unexempted detour (F1, F3).
The driver's hearing of 'no objection' and the unread request (F8) may be read as tacit acceptance by silence, though RD-5 requires agreement before the deviation begins.
The rider's own 90-day record includes 2 disputes with 0 upheld, which the driver may use to paint the complaint as routine (F13).

claims.assertion: The trip had exactly one off-route segment: 18:32–18:39, 3.32 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km of extra distance.
The driver asked the rider in-app at 18:28 — before the 18:32 detour began — whether he could go round via Outram Road, so the change was raised before leaving the optimal route.

The rider never replied to the 18:28 route request, so the chat record contains no express agreement to the Outram Road routing; consent therefore fails the 'explicit agreement before the detour' test.

The driver's justification for rerouting was traffic on Kampong Bahru Road, but the only traffic records in the trip window are NEW BRIDGE ROAD and SENTOSA GATEWAY at speed band 3, and no traffic incidents were recorded near the route, so there is no traffic evidence for the substituted stretch of the optimal route.
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the extra 2.21 km on the unexempted segment directly entered the metered distance charge at $1.41/km.
The refund properly payable on the unexempted segment is 2.21 km × $1.41/km = $3.12 (rounded to the cent), being the meter distance units generated by the detour and nothing else.
The remaining excess billed ($4.21 for 3.0 km) includes the ≤0.25 km map-matching residual over and above the 2.21 km of identified detour, and it must not be refunded.
There was no waiting charge and no surge on this trip, and no unannounced post-trip add-on was appended, so no further line item falls to be refunded.
No cooling-off or traffic justification applies to the post-18:32 portion of the detour either: the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so no weather-based excuse is available.
The driver has 752 trips in 90 days and a 90-day dispute history of 0 upheld route deviations, so this is not a repeated route-deviation case and no account flag is warranted against the driver.

weaknesses: The rider's own version in the complaint (no reply, higher fare than estimate) is corroborated by the system records, and the driver's statement at F8 ('no objection, so I took it') is directly contradicted by the absence of any agreement message in F7 — silence is not consent under RD-5, so the core finding against the driver is hard to resist.

F3 shows a detour that strayed up to 1262 m from the optimal route for 7 minutes, far beyond map-matching noise, so the driver cannot characterise the 2.21 km as a measurement artefact; the best realistic position is only to cap the refund at $3.12 rather than the full $4.21 excess billed at F4.

F7's timestamp (18:28) is before the detour start (18:32), which the other side will argue shows the driver consciously chose the reroute expecting agreement; the driver can only answer that there was never an express 'yes'.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $3.12 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered service [F6], and the fact table records exactly one off-route segment, 18:32-18:39, driving 3.32 km where the optimal route covers 1.10 km and adding 2.21 km [F3]. Under RD-1 each off-route segment is reviewed individually, and an unexplained deviation breaches the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty; here the total is 10.9 km vs 7.9 km optimal, +3.0 km (+38%) [F1], so the deviation is real and substantial. [RD-1]

No exemption applies. The driver's pre-departure message at 18:28 asked ok if I go round via Outram Road? [F7], but RD-5 requires the rider's agreement to be timestamped before the segment start (18:32) [F3]; the rider never replied, so there is no consent, and the driver's own statement that there was no objection [F8] is a statement of belief that cannot override the chat record [F7]. Silence is not the mutual agreement RD-5 demands, and the consent scope does not extend to a route the rider never affirmatively accepted. [RD-5]

The traffic justification also fails. RD-4 requires a qualifying incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route, and no incident was recorded near the route during the trip window [F11]; the only speed-band readings are band 3 (20-29 km/h) on NEW BRIDGE ROAD [F9] and SENTOSA GATEWAY [F10], which are neither at band 1-2 nor shown to be the substituted stretch, so by RD-4(c) the segment falls to RD-2. Fair weather, 0.0 mm rain [F12], removes any weather excuse. [RD-4]

Because this is RydeTAXI, the extra mileage directly entered the metered distance charge [F6], so RD-2 applies: refund = the unexempted extra_km times the trip per-km rate, where the rate = distance fare divided by distance km = $15.33 / 10.9 km = $1.40642/km, applied by the execution trace at $1.4103/km [F4][F6]. Thus 2.21 km x $1.4103/km = $3.1168, rounded to $3.12. Only the unexempted segment's mileage is refundable; the residual between the billed 3.0 km excess ($4.21 for 3.0 km x $1.41/km) [F1][F4] and the 2.21 km identified detour [F3] is map-matching residue and is not refunded under RD-2. [RD-2]

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's 90-day history shows 0 upheld route disputes [F14], so the case is not repeated and no flag_account attaches; the rider's own 2 disputes / 0 upheld [F13] does not bear on whether this deviation is exempted. The refund is payable as a Ryde voucher per NS-7 [F6]. [RD-6][NS-7]

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your dispute and you get a $3.12 Ryde voucher. One part of your trip was off the most direct route: between 18:32 and 18:39 the driver took a longer way, adding about 2.2 km that we could not excuse. We asked if the driver had your agreement for that route segment, and the record shows a message was sent but you never replied, so there was no consent, and there was no traffic incident recorded on the stretch that would have justified it. Since your fare was metered, that extra distance went into what you paid. The voucher is issued to your account and can be used on future Ryde trips. No action is being taken against the driver's account.

DRIVER: We reviewed a route dispute on one of your metered trips. One segment was found to be off the most direct route, and no exemption applied: the message you sent asking about going round via that road was not answered before the segment began, so there was no rider agreement, and no traffic incident was recorded on the stretch that would have justified the route. A $3.12 Ryde voucher has been issued to the rider for the extra distance you drove on that segment. No action has been taken against your account. Keep asking before varying from the shortest route and wait for a clear yes before the trip continues.

what_would_change: Had an LTA incident been recorded on the stretch F3 replaced, before it started, RD-4 would exempt it (−$3.12).
Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.

claims.assertion: The trip ran 10.9 km against a 7.9 km optimal route (+3.0 km, +38%) and included one off-route segment 18:32–18:39 that drove 3.32 km where the optimal route covers 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km and straying up to 1262 m from the optimal route.

The driver asked at 18:28 'ok if I go round via Outram Road?' and the rider never replied; under RD-5 an unanswered route-change proposal is not consent, and the request timestamp precedes the off-route segment's start, so the segment is not exempted.

The driver's written justification ('no objection, so I took it') rests only on the rider's silence, which contradicts the chat record showing no rider agreement message at all; silence does not satisfy 'reach a mutual agreement before you go'.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only speed-band readings (New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway, band 3 = 20–29 km/h) are not on the substituted optimal route at band 1 or 2, so no RD-4 exemption applies to the unexempted segment.

RydeTAXI bills by the meter, so the 2.21 km of unexempted deviation distance is chargeable detour mileage; at this trip's own per-km rate (distance fare $15.33 ÷ 10.9 km = $1.4064/km) the refund is 2.21 × $1.4064 ≈ $3.11, and the rider's recoverable excess distance billed is $4.21 (3.0 km × $1.41/km).
The complaint is timely and 30 days have not elapsed, and the refund is payable as a Ryde voucher per NS-7.
The driver's account (185 days old, rating 4.5, 2 disputes in 90 days) shows no upheld route dispute, so the additional flag_account of RD-6 is not triggered here.

weaknesses: RD-2's non-metered/metered split hinges on the service being RydeTAXI; if the trip were re-classified as a fixed-quote service, the recoverable amount would fall to the ERP/toll excess on the deviation segment only (F4, F6).

The deviation is a single 7-minute segment in an area with heavy evening congestion (F11 shows no incidents, but F9/F10 show band 3 roads at 20–29 km/h near the corridor); the driver may argue some of the extra distance was unavoidable (F8, F9, F11).

The +3.0 km total excess exceeds the 2.21 km of the single off-route segment by ~0.79 km, and the driver could argue the remainder falls within map-matching residue rather than an unexempted detour (F1, F3).
The driver's hearing of 'no objection' and the unread request (F8) may be read as tacit acceptance by silence, though RD-5 requires agreement before the deviation begins.
The rider's own 90-day record includes 2 disputes with 0 upheld, which the driver may use to paint the complaint as routine (F13).

claims.assertion: The trip had exactly one off-route segment: 18:32–18:39, 3.32 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.10 km, adding 2.21 km of extra distance.
The driver asked the rider in-app at 18:28 — before the 18:32 detour began — whether he could go round via Outram Road, so the change was raised before leaving the optimal route.

The rider never replied to the 18:28 route request, so the chat record contains no express agreement to the Outram Road routing; consent therefore fails the 'explicit agreement before the detour' test.

The driver's justification for rerouting was traffic on Kampong Bahru Road, but the only traffic records in the trip window are NEW BRIDGE ROAD and SENTOSA GATEWAY at speed band 3, and no traffic incidents were recorded near the route, so there is no traffic evidence for the substituted stretch of the optimal route.
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the extra 2.21 km on the unexempted segment directly entered the metered distance charge at $1.41/km.
The refund properly payable on the unexempted segment is 2.21 km × $1.41/km = $3.12 (rounded to the cent), being the meter distance units generated by the detour and nothing else.
The remaining excess billed ($4.21 for 3.0 km) includes the ≤0.25 km map-matching residual over and above the 2.21 km of identified detour, and it must not be refunded.
There was no waiting charge and no surge on this trip, and no unannounced post-trip add-on was appended, so no further line item falls to be refunded.
No cooling-off or traffic justification applies to the post-18:32 portion of the detour either: the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain, so no weather-based excuse is available.
The driver has 752 trips in 90 days and a 90-day dispute history of 0 upheld route deviations, so this is not a repeated route-deviation case and no account flag is warranted against the driver.

weaknesses: The rider's own version in the complaint (no reply, higher fare than estimate) is corroborated by the system records, and the driver's statement at F8 ('no objection, so I took it') is directly contradicted by the absence of any agreement message in F7 — silence is not consent under RD-5, so the core finding against the driver is hard to resist.

F3 shows a detour that strayed up to 1262 m from the optimal route for 7 minutes, far beyond map-matching noise, so the driver cannot characterise the 2.21 km as a measurement artefact; the best realistic position is only to cap the refund at $3.12 rather than the full $4.21 excess billed at F4.

F7's timestamp (18:28) is before the detour start (18:32), which the other side will argue shows the driver consciously chose the reroute expecting agreement; the driver can only answer that there was never an express 'yes'.

points.response: Accepted as far as it goes: F3 identifies one off-route segment adding 2.21 km, and that segment alone is unexempted, but the trip total still shows +3.0 km and +38% over the optimal route (F1), so the single segment is the floor, not the whole measure of the deviation.
The 18:28 message is only a [request] (F7), and the driver's own statement admits the rider never said anything (F8); a question is not the mutual agreement RD-5 requires.

Conceded on the point of law — the rider gave no express agreement — and that concession disposes of the driver's own defence, since RD-5 requires the agreement before departure and silence cannot supply it.

Agreed, and this defeats any RD-4 exemption: the only speed records are band 3 (20–29 km/h) on New Bridge Road and Sentosa Gateway (F9, F10), neither of which is the substituted Kampong Bahru Road section, and no incident was recorded near the route (F11).

Accepted: RydeTAXI is metered (F6), so the 2.21 km of unexempted detour mileage entered the distance charge at this trip's own rate of $1.4064/km, not merely at the flat $1.41 figure the driver quotes.

The driver's $3.12 uses a $1.41/km rate, but the correct per-km rate is derived from the fare itself ($15.33 ÷ 10.9 km = $1.4064), giving 2.21 × $1.4064 = $3.11; and the rider's alternative measure, the actual excess distance billed of $4.21 (F4), remains the amount the meter over-collected.

The rider accepts the ≤0.25 km residual is not refundable, but the unexplained remainder here is 0.79 km (F1 minus F3), far above 0.25 km and unexplained by the driver, so RD-2 offers no basis for writing it off without evidence.
Agreed that no waiting fee, surge (F5) or undisclosed post-trip add-on appears in the breakdown, so the refund is confined to the detour mileage.

Irrelevant but unhelpful to the driver: fair weather (F12) removes any weather excuse, and the absence of any incident record (F11) removes the traffic excuse, leaving the deviation wholly unexempted under RD-4.
Agreed on the 90-day history: the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes (F14), so RD-6's flag_account is not triggered and the rider does not seek an account flag.

Conceded: F1 and F3 establish the +3.0 km overall excess and the single 2.21 km off-route segment, and RD-1 imposes the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty without any percentage threshold, so the segment stands as an unexempted deviation.
Conceded: F7 shows the rider never answered the 18:28 request and F3 shows the segment began at 18:32, so there is no agreement timestamped before the deviation as RD-5 requires.
Conceded: F8 is a post-hoc statement of the driver's own belief and, per the system-record priority rule, it cannot override the chat record at F7 which contains no rider agreement at all.
